data.title: Meduza: Estonia is closing one of the last major land routes between Europe and Russia. Here’s what the drivers and passengers who depend on it have to say.
data.summary: Starting December 1, Estonia will close all five of its border crossings with Russia for at least six months. The crossings were used by many Russian emigres and tourists, as well as residents of the Baltic states and Finland who travel to Russia to see family or for work. Over the past few years, an entire industry has grown up around these crossings, with numerous firms and private drivers taking passengers to the checkpoints on both the Estonian and Russian sides. The independent journalist cooperative Bereg spoke with drivers and their clients about how the route through Estonia into Russia worked and what they plan to do once the border closes. Meduza is publishing the piece in full.

data.title: Meduza: Moscow high society: celebrities pose for photos in front of giant ‘STALIN’ sign. Scenes from the premiere of a new Russian miniseries about the Soviet dictator.
data.summary: Director Vladimir Bortko has made a six-part feature film called Stalin. The first episodes will premiere on the Kion streaming service on November 26, with a television premiere on REN TV set for December 6. Bortko reportedly worked on the project for 15 years, and the script is based on declassified documents and memoirs. The story takes place between 1945 and 1953, the year Joseph Stalin died. The filmmakers promise to show “not good or bad, but the truth,” but judging by the trailer, it’s a typical Russian “patriotic blockbuster” in which a resolute leader stands up to the West. Stalin is played by Igor Mirkurbanov, an actor who has mostly played antiheroes onstage, including the Pretender in Boris Godunov and the elder Karamazov in The Karamazovs. The film also stars Viktor Sukhorukov as Khrushchev and Alexander Yatsko as Beria. On November 23, a society premiere of the film was held at Moscow’s Khudozhestvenny movie theater, where invited Russian celebrities posed for photos in front of a press wall bearing the word “STALIN.” Take a look at these photos.
